input.question: How did O.J. Simpson win the trial of the century?
input.ground_truth: The evidence was all circumstantial. They couldn't place him at the scene, it all pointed at him but none of it was conclusive. The one thing they did have was some blood that was sure win except DNA evidence was largely new at the time so the lawyers were able to convince the jury that it was mishandled and couldn't be accurate. Also they played the race card hard. They made it look like it was the white system just looking for another guilty black man. In the end its truly messed up because the book he wrote is essentially a confession and how to get away with murder for dummies.

Okay, let’s imagine there’s a big game of “Did you do it?” with a famous person named O.J. Simpson. Lots of people thought he might have done something very bad, like hurting two people a long time ago.

So, there was a group of people called a “jury.” Their job was to listen to everything and decide if O.J. did it or not. Lawyers for both sides told stories and showed things to help the jury decide.

Even though many people thought O.J. probably did it, the jury listened to all the stories and the rules very carefully. At the end, they decided that the people who were trying to prove he did it didn’t show it “for sure.” So, the jury said, “We can’t be 100% sure he did it,” and they said he was not guilty.

That’s how O.J. Simpson won the trial, even though lots of people still think he probably did it.
